item: newgame-screen (+ keep awake): New-game screen order, one row per option, compact rows, a clearer bot icon, and a screen that stays on
summary: The order is now ranked 2, 3 and 4, then practice against a bot, then solo practice. This is set in MODE_OPTIONS and AVAILABLE_MODES in homeModel.ts, and the same order shows on screen. In ModesScreen.tsx the wide/pair split and the `compact` prop are gone, so every option is a full-width row with a chevron and a one-line tagline, ranked 3 and 4 included. The rows are smaller and use tokens only. The title is 18 (sheetTitle), as DECISIONS prefers; it was h1 22. Card padding is 6 vertical and 12 horizontal, with a 12 gap and minHeight 64. Content padding is 8 at the top and 16 at the bottom, with a 16 gap; the group gap is 8. The title and tagline have no extra gap, and the chips sit 2 under the tagline. A row is now 77 dp. A new test reads the rendered styles and checks the budget: on a 360×780 phone, assuming a status bar of at most 32 and 3-button navigation (48), the header (56) leaves 644 dp. Six rows plus the footnote need 622 dp in Hebrew and 638 dp in English (the footnote takes two lines there), so they fit without scrolling. The ScrollView stays as the fallback, and there is no card for staged practice. The `bot` glyph in Icon.tsx is redrawn with a mouth, solid eyes twice as large, an antenna ball and ears. I rendered it with canvaskit to check it by eye at 11–96 px. On the Modes card it shows in a new BotLead: a 44 frame (radius 14, border 2) in P2's ring colour on surface2, with the robot at 28 in P2. The same glyph also changes TimeoutView's 'bot' button and the results' bot-opponents card. Keep-awake: expo-keep-awake ~57.0.2 is now a direct dependency of apps/mobile. The lockfile change is one line, added by hand; npm ls shows it as direct and deduped. A new config `displayConfig.keepScreenOn` (default true) is in config/display.ts. The new hook `useKeepScreenOn` in services/keepAwake.ts loads the module lazily and uses its own tag, 'sudoku-fight'. It takes the tag again each time the app comes to the foreground, which covers a start-up call that fails because the Activity is not ready yet. It releases the tag on unmount and never lets an error reach the app. RootLayout calls it before the fontsReady early return, so it is on for the whole app from the first frame. Docs are updated: 01-SPEC §5.1 and §22, the QA checklist (row 7 and a new 'how to test' step 8), components.md §0.4 and §2, and DECISIONS-PENDING 3.23.

item: matchmaking: "find opponent" with nobody else searching. The server's `searching` and `timeout` messages carry `nextRange` (null means nobody else to meet), and the app says so right away.
summary:
The protocol now has `rangeCovering(distance, extended, rules)`. It gives the narrowest D6 range that covers a rating distance, clamped to the cap unless the search is extended. Both `searching` and `timeout` carry an optional `nextRange?: number | null`, and the flow comment explains it.

The matcher has two new pure functions: `recentMap()`, extracted from `matchTick()` with no change in behaviour, and `nextRanges(tickets, groupSize, config)` (rule 7). For each ticket, rule 7 takes the players it could actually meet: groupSize−1 of them, in the same queue, not blocked either way, within both maximum ranges, and not a recent opponent after the 80% reset. It returns the rangeCovering of the farthest one needed, or null when there are not enough of them.

`MatchQueue` keeps a version counter, bumped by add, remove and any tick that takes tickets out. It memoises the ranges per version and adds `nextRange(userId)` and `nextRangeOf(ticket)`. The second is for a ticket that just timed out.

The service sends `nextRange` in every `searching`. On each tick it sends `searching` again when the range or the next range changed, so a player learns within about 500 ms that someone joined or left. The `timeout` message carries `nextRangeOf()`.

The app client mirrors `nextRange` into `SearchInfo` and `TimeoutInfo`. An older server leaves it undefined, and keepSearching keeps the last value. The screen model gets `alone` on both the search and timeout screens.

SearchView shows the alone notice right away instead of the range card, the "widening" note and the "avoiding recent opponents" note. The notice is the title "כרגע אין שחקנים אחרים שמחפשים משחק כזה", a body, and a "שחק מול בוט בינתיים" button. The radar, clock, empty seats and cancel button keep running, and the screen reader hears the alone title once. TimeoutView uses its own alone title and body and drops "בלי הגבלת טווח". MatchScreen's `toBot` (cancel, then onBot) is shared by both views.

D6 widening and the 60 s timeout are unchanged, and nothing jumps to the next range. All strings are in he and en, with Hebrew plural forms for tables of 3–4. Docs are updated.

item: rating-refresh: the rating, XP, level, league and card stats now update after a ranked game without restarting the app
summary: Implemented the design client-only, with no server or protocol change. OnlineSession has a new onEnd({state, playerId, left}) callback. It fires once at gameOver, next to the game_end analytics, and from close() when the game is still running (left: true). It is wrapped in try/catch. The game store wires it in both session constructions (goOnline, goRanked's enter) via the new GameStoreDeps.onlineEnd, whose default is progress/appProgress onlineGameEnded. The new pure game/rankedEnd.ts turns a state into a RankedEnd, or null for unrated, dev, practice or non-member cases: rankedEndOf for a game that is over, rankedLeftOf for leaving a running 2-player rated game (waits graceMs plus a margin), and storedIn (the server's games in the key > gamesBefore). The new progress/rankedRefresh.ts (class RankedRefresh, timers injected) does three things. It shows the server-computed rating at once through authStore.showRankedResult (in memory, plus a pending entry with a TTL). It polls fetchMe on accountConfig.refresh.afterRanked.confirmDelaysMs until storedIn, then calls refreshMyProgress once. It also handles unrated ends, dedup by gameId, a 'left' wait being superseded, and stop(). authStore got these additions: AuthDeps.now; module state for pendingRatings, lastServerReadAt and the request seq/in-flight counters (reset in setAuthDeps, forgetLocal and every needsProfile); adopt() merging pending ratings via api/me withPendingRatings while caching the raw server Me; and the new exports fetchMe(), refreshMeIfStale() and showRankedResult(). refreshMe() is now a wrapper over fetchMe, with the same signature. Home's focus effect calls refreshMeIfStale(), which reads at most every 30 s and at once when the profile came from the cache. The app's foreground handler also calls it, and startProgress stops the ranked refresh on sign-out, an owner change, and its own stop. All tunables are in accountConfig.refresh. Tests cover the pure helpers, RankedRefresh with ManualScheduler, the session and store wiring, the authStore merge/TTL/throttle/seq guard/sign-out, appProgress, Home focus, and two new ranked e2e scenarios: 'לבית' before the server stored the game (never flips back to 1200), and leaving results with router.back(). The docs are updated: SPEC §4.3 and §12, the device checks, the QA, release and pending-decisions files.

refreshMeIfStale also skips while a GET /v1/me is in flight (meInFlight counter). This avoids a double read when the results' leave() refreshMe and Home's focus run together.

fetchMe drops the answer when the status is no longer 'ready', not only when the uid changed. Its notRegistered → needsProfile path now applies only if the same uid is still signed in. adopt(), when called outside fetchMe (initAuth, PATCH, registration), marks every read still in flight as stale (seq defaults to meRequests).
forgetRefreshState does not reset the request counters. It sets meAdopted = meRequests, so reads still in flight are never adopted.

item: penalty: a wrong digit costs the points the right digit would have scored there at that moment (replaces the 1, 2, 4, 8 ladder; D14 closed)
summary: I implemented Moshe's new mistake rule across engine, protocol, server, mobile, fixtures and docs. The engine charges a wrong digit with `missedPoints(grid, cell, solutionDigit, rules.scoreY).points`: the §6.4 formula on the board before the entry, 1.5–13.5, not tied to the mistake number. The helper `wrongDigitPenalty` in engine.ts does this. `rules.mistakePenalty: 'missedPoints' | 'doubling'` replaces `mistakePenaltyCap`, with 'missedPoints' as the default in every mode. The old ladder is still available as `doublingPenalty(k)` under 'doubling', and the D14 cap is gone. item: givens: starting givens per game type (fast 45–50, normal 35–40, hard unchanged)
summary: The cause was the puzzle data, not routing: the generator removed givens down to 22 for every type, so fast and normal boards looked as sparse as hard ones. The engine now has a rule, DEFAULT_GIVENS (packages/engine/src/sudoku/givens.ts): fast 45–50, normal 35–40, and hard null. Hard is null because DECISIONS.md, updated during the run, says Moshe asked that hard boards stay exactly as they are; the design's 24–28 range for hard is gone. Two pure, seeded functions do the fill. addGivens gives each new given to the digit with the fewest givens, in the box with the fewest givens, and never adds a given that would make the puzzle easier than its type. fitGivens returns noRange, inRange, filled, tooMany or gradeLost. fitBankGivens(bank) seeds each puzzle from seedFromString(id, salt); a filled puzzle gets a new id, a new grade and baseId = its old id. The result is deterministic, independent of order, and running it again changes nothing. A new script, npm run puzzles:givens [-- --dry-run], rewrote packages/engine/data/puzzles.json: all 2690 fast puzzles are now 45–50 (digit spread ≤2) and normal puzzles 35–40 (spread ≤3, all 9 digits, still needing a hidden single). The 2300 hard puzzles are byte-identical to HEAD. 7 normal puzzles (6 ranked, 1 offline) could not keep their grade and were replaced with the generator (seeds 20261015 and 20261017), so the bank still has 2000 ranked and 300 offline per type. The generator and the importer now output in-range puzzles, so re-importing the CSV adds no duplicates (tested). apps/mobile/src/game/data/offline-puzzles.json was regenerated. On the server, a new migration 0007_retired_puzzles adds puzzles.retired_at. db:seed-puzzles marks ranked puzzles that left the file as retired instead of deleting them, a puzzle that returns to the file is un-retired, and a type with no ranked puzzles in the file is left alone. rankedPool and rankedPoolSizes skip retired puzzles. The new rankedPoolMatches makes --if-empty (and so dev:lan) reseed when the bank changed. A run of the seed script against a scratch PGlite (old bank, then the new one) retired 2000 fast and 2000 normal puzzles, 0 hard. Docs are updated: spec §5.2, §6.4 (re-measured points), §19, §20 and §24 (D5 text, new row D43 ✓), plus QA-CHECKLIST, DECISIONS-PENDING (new closed item 2.15 and a note in 1.8), README, DEPLOY-PRODUCTION §7, MOSHE-TODO (new D5b, and a note in D12), ASSET-LICENSES §4 and the work plan.
